# RuDao (儒道) — Beyond The Art of War
# By Tony Tong (唐仪)
# https://rudao.us/ | https://TonyTong.cc

## About This Book

RuDao (儒道) is a bilingual (English / 中文) business philosophy book by Tony Tong (唐仪), subtitled "RuJiang: Beyond The Art of War — The Confucian Co-opetition Path to Balanced Profit and Enduring Partnerships."

The book is structured in six chapters, framed by Front Matter (0) and Back Matter (7):
- Ch. 1: The Roots 源 — Natural Pursuit of Profit 人性趋利, from 1600 BCE
- Ch. 2: The Confucian Core 儒 — Righteousness + Profit, Harmony vs Co-opetition
- Ch. 3: Ru + Dao 内圣外王 — Inner Sage, Outer King
- Ch. 4: Inner Sage, Outer King, and the RuJiang 内圣外王 · 儒将
- Ch. 5: RuShang Practice 实践 — The Way of the Confucian Merchant
- Ch. 6: RuDao in the AI Digital Age 数字时代

## Core Thesis

For 2,500 years, strategists have studied Sun Tzu's *The Art of War* (孙子兵法) as the bible of business competition — teaching leaders how to defeat rivals. But zero-sum thinking erodes trust and makes enduring partnerships impossible.

*RuDao* moves beyond adversarial strategy. It unfolds the Confucian path of co-opetition (竞合之道): profit and meaningful relationships are not trade-offs. You can compete fiercely while building stable, lasting partnerships.

## Three Core Principles

1. **义利共存 — Profit & Trust Coexist**: Profit need not sacrifice trust; righteousness and profit are unified.
2. **竞合并行 — Competition & Cooperation in Parallel**: Compete where the market is real; cooperate where value is shared.
3. **共赢联盟 — Win-Win Alliances**: True victory is not defeating everyone, but growing the pie together.

## Author

Tony Tong (唐仪) is a global cross-border entrepreneur, seasoned investor, and business strategist. He is:
- Co-founder of the Hong Kong Blockchain Association (HKBA)
- Adjunct professor at ITU.edu, University of Minnesota, PolyU, and HKFSI
- US Patent No. 6,012,066 holder (Internet workflow system)
- Frequent speaker at UBS, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, CLSA, Jeffries, Roth Capital, G2E, GITEX, Consensus, Korea Blockchain Week, Economist, and Forbes
- Creator of the 儒将竞合战略 (Ru-Jiang co-opetition framework)

## Lineage

RuDao braids three traditions:
- 儒商 (Confucian Merchant) — commerce with integrity
- 儒将 (Confucian General) — power tempered by learning
- 天人合一 (Unity of Heaven & Humanity) — Taoist root

## Comparison: Art of War vs RuDao

- Core logic: Zero-sum → Positive-sum
- Rival relationship: Defeat → Make partner
- Time horizon: Short-term victory → Sustainable partnerships
- Strategic posture: Deception → Trust & transparency
- View of profit: Maximize own gain → Balanced, shared value
- Ethical frame: Utility → Virtue as strategy
- Ultimate goal: Win the war → Build the alliance

## 7.4 Source Note — The Classic of WeiQi/Go (Qi Jing 棋经十三篇)

At the end of 7.4 Sources & References, a framed source note (The Origin 经典出处与原文字源) documents the provenance of the Go quotation used in RuDao's co-opetition chapters: Zhang Ni 张拟, Scholar of the Hanlin Academy 翰林学士, Song Dynasty (北宋皇祐年间, c. 1049-1054 CE), author of the Qi Jing Shi San Pian 《棋经十三篇》(the first systematic theory of Go, often called the Art of War of Go), Lun Ju 论局篇: "善胜者不争，善败者不乱" — those who excel at winning do not contend, those who excel at losing do not lose order.

In the same 7.4 bibliography, the "Civilization Conversations 文明对话" list also records "The Song Flying out of Haibuwutian" 《从海武田飞出的歌》 — the biographical account of Tong Cho Sam 唐楚三 (Tang ChuSan), Hong Kong industrialist and father of the author, co-authored by Qin Zhong and Chen Yanru 秦忠、陈妍如, published by Guangxi Ethnic Publishing House 广西民族出版社, 1995.

## 7.2 Appendix A — Wall of Ru-Shang Aphorisms 儒商格言墙

The opening "Wall of Ru-Shang (儒商 Confucian Merchant) Aphorisms 儒商格言墙" in 7.2 Appendix A · Classified Index of Quotes gathers 25 bilingual aphorisms (English + 原文): Confucius 孔子 (仁者爱人, 见利思义, 君子怀德小人怀利, 君子易事而难说, 其身正不令而行, 工欲善其事必先利其器, 德不孤必有邻, 君子喻于义小人喻于利), the classics (The Great Learning 大学 仁者以财发身 / 修身齐家治国平天下 / 苟日新日日新, The Book of Rites 礼记 信者事之本也, I Ching 易经 天行健君子以自强不息), the early RuShang 儒商先贤 (Zigong 子贡 先修其德而后营其事 / 信以通商久交之本 / 君子之威源于德, Fan Li 范蠡 富好行其德, Fan Li (Tao Zhu Gong) 范蠡（陶朱公）贵出如粪土贱取如珠玉, Bai Gui 白圭 人弃我取人取我予, Ji Ran 计然 旱则资舟水则资车, Guan Zhong 管仲 明主审时顺人心 / 和则能聚争则能进, Xunzi 荀子 积善成德而神明自得), plus Mencius 孟子 得道者多助 and Sun Tzu 孙子 知彼知己百战不殆.
